subject: Budget range validation - Skyline Finance
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@skyline-finance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Budget range validation - Skyline Finance

Hi Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and two asks so we can align the commercials: 

1) Volume/Band: You mentioned expected production usage of 40-120M generated tokens/month after Q3 ramp (with spikes). For qualification I captured an initial monthly spend band of roughly $15k-$40k/month on hosted API. Please confirm if that still sounds right.

2) Procurement thresholds: you said POs below $50k are handled by Operations; anything >= $75k goes to Legal/Finance review and requires an enterprise SOW. Can you confirm those thresholds (PO min / legal review trigger)?

Unit economics note (for context): our public hosted list pricing is approximately $350 / 1M generated tokens (equivalent to $0.00035/token); with a committed reserved capacity we can get toward ~$200 / 1M depending on term and bandwidth.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the monthly spend band and procurement triggers (reply to this thread).
- If the band is >$25k/month we can propose a 3-month pilot + committed tier to hit the lower $/1M.
- I'll loop in Marissa (AM) to draft a short pilot agreement and Rishi for any approval on discounting.

Attaching the one-pager pricing sheet we walked through: pricing-sheet-skyline.pdf (PDF, 42KB).

Thanks — talk soon.

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@skyline-finance.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lucas Park <lucas.park@skyline-finance.com>, procurement@skyline-finance.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Skyline Finance

Thanks for the recap, Dylan — that matches most of what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Estimated monthly spend band (post-ramp): right now leadership is modeling $15k-$30k/month for the first 6 months, with a potential to move toward $40k+ if we expand to more users. The $15k figure reflects a conservative rollout.
- Procurement thresholds: procurement@skyline-finance.com can issue POs up to $50k without exec approval. Anything above $50k requires a formal procurement sign-off and >$75k triggers legal review per CFO guidance.
- Trial needs: we'd prefer a 60-day pilot with a modest cap and an initial credit while we validate quality and latency for our use cases.

Question for you: is the $200 / 1M token number something you can commit to for a 6-12 month reserved commitment at a specific monthly spend? Or is that only for large annual commits? Also can you confirm any per-request latency/throughput SLOs for the hosted option — that's a gating factor for our front-end team.

If helpful, looping in Lucas (CFO) for procurement/contract thresholds — Lucas, happy to connect separately if helpful.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform, Skyline Finance
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Budget range validation - Skyline Finance

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Alex's reply. Key asks: 60-day pilot, confirm procurement thresholds (PO up to $50k; >$75k -> legal), and whether we can offer a committed $/1M token of ~$200 for a 6-12 month monthly commit in the ~$25k+ band.

Suggested options we should propose back: 
- Pilot (60 days): hosted API, $5k account credit, pilot cap 150k tokens/day (~4.5M tokens/month). No legal SOW; PO or standard T&Cs only.
- Committed monthly tier (3-12 month): $25k/month commit -> effective ~$200 / 1M tokens (assumes ~125M tokens/month equivalent to that spend), with a step-down pricing grid as volume grows.
- Hosted pay-as-you-go: $350 / 1M tokens list.

Rishi — can you confirm discounting authority we have here? If we need approval to land the committed $200 / 1M for a 6-month term I can flag this as a deal needing 20-30% off list. Marissa — can you prep a pilot agreement (short) and include required pilot caps and data handling notes. I attached our internal pricing model for reference: internal-pricing-models.xlsx (XLSX, 64KB).

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@skyline-finance.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@skyline-finance.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Budget range validation - Skyline Finance

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and helpful context. Confirming next steps and two commercial paths we can offer for Skyline to evaluate: 

1) 60-day pilot (recommended first step)
   - Hosted API access, up to 150k generated tokens/day (cumulative cap ~4.5M tokens/month).
   - $5k pilot credit applied up front (covers early usage).
   - Standard Redwood T&Cs; procurement can provide a PO for the pilot (POs < $50k OK).

2) Committed monthly tier (best unit economics)
   - Example: $25k/month commit -> equivalent ~125M tokens/month (dependent on prompt lengths) -> target rate ~ $200 / 1M generated tokens.
   - 3-12 month term options; longer terms reduce $/1M.
   - If monthly commit expected to exceed $50k we'll surface enterprise procurement workflow; >$75k triggers legal SOW review per your internal rules.

Hosted pay-as-you-go remains available at list ~$350 / 1M tokens if you prefer no commit.

Pilot logistics / next steps:
- I can draft the short pilot agreement and the trial config (caps, telemetry access, success metrics) — see draft: redwood-pilot-agreement.docx (DOCX, 18KB).
- If you confirm pilot, procurement can issue a PO (we'll accept PO < $50k).
- If you're leaning toward commit, let us know target monthly commit and term and we'll put together a commercial term sheet (we may need Rishi's approval for any >20% discount off list).

Link to the pilot template and next steps doc: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/pilot-template

Looking forward — happy to jump on a short call to finalize pilot details.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
